tool.hash-identify.context.locked: the leading "!" means the account is locked; the hash itself is intact
tool.hash-identify.context.noHash: this account has no password hash (locked, or password login disabled)
tool.hash-identify.description: Tell which hash a string is (MD5, NTLM, bcrypt, sha512crypt, Kerberos...) and get the hashcat and John names.
tool.hash-identify.error.empty: Paste a hash to identify, or several hashes one per line.
tool.hash-identify.format.crack-the-4th-: Crack the 4th field as NTLM; the 3rd is LM (aad3b435b51404ee… = disabled)
tool.hash-identify.format.crack-the-seco: Crack the second half as NTLM. aad3b435b51404ee… means LM is disabled
tool.hash-identify.format.default-etc-sh: Default /etc/shadow hash on most Linux distributions
tool.hash-identify.format.default-in-rec: Default in recent Debian / Ubuntu / Fedora shadow files. John only
tool.hash-identify.format.drop-the-bcryp: Drop the "bcrypt$" prefix first (bcrypt_sha256 pre-hashes the password)
tool.hash-identify.format.first-2-charac: First 2 characters are the salt. Only the first 8 password characters count
tool.hash-identify.format.mysql5-hashes-: MySQL5 hashes are written *HEX in capitals; add the *
tool.hash-identify.format.slow-by-design: Slow by design: use a targeted wordlist
tool.hash-identify.format.two-independen: Two independent 7-character halves, so each half is cracked separately
tool.hash-identify.format.use-the-jwt-to: Use the JWT tool to decode, verify, forge or crack it
tool.hash-identify.format.windows-nt-has: Windows NT hash: MD4 of the UTF-16LE password
tool.hash-identify.known.lm-half-of-the-: LM half of the empty password
tool.hash-identify.known.lm-of-the-empty: LM of the empty password (LM is disabled)
tool.hash-identify.name: Hash identifier
tool.hash-identify.note.jwt: This is a JSON Web Token: use the JWT tool to decode it, try alg none or crack a weak secret.
tool.hash-identify.note.noMatch: {label}: no known hash format matches ({shape}). It may be truncated, salted in an unusual way, encoded (try Base64 / Hex) or not a hash at all.
tool.hash-identify.note.tooMany: Paste {max} lines or fewer to see every candidate for each hash.
tool.hash-identify.note.truncated_one: Only the first {max} of {count} lines were analysed.
tool.hash-identify.note.truncated_other: Only the first {max} of {count} lines were analysed.
tool.hash.description: MD5, SHA-1/2/3, NTLM, RIPEMD, BLAKE, Whirlpool, CRC32 and more in one run, with HMAC and compare.
tool.hash.error.notHex: The expected hash is not hex or Base64. Paste just the digest, e.g. {example}.
tool.hash.name: Hash / checksum
tool.hash.note.newline: Not an exact match, but {names} matches with {what}. (echo adds a newline: use echo -n.)
tool.hash.note.noMatchSameSizeHmac: No match. The expected value has {size}, like {names}, so the input probably differs (salt, encoding, extra whitespace), or it is an HMAC: set an HMAC key.
tool.hash.note.noMatchSameSizeKey: No match. The expected value has {size}, like {names}, so the input probably differs (salt, encoding, extra whitespace) or the key is wrong.
tool.hash.note.noMatchSize: No match. {size} is not the size of any algorithm here. Is the hash truncated, or a different family (bcrypt, crypt, ...)? Try the Hash identifier.
tool.hash.options.expected.hint: Hex or Base64. Tells you which algorithm (and HMAC) produces exactly this value.
tool.hash.options.expected.label: Compare with
tool.hash.options.expected.placeholder: paste a known hash to find its algorithm
tool.hash.options.hmacKey.label: HMAC key
tool.hash.options.keyHex.hint: Read the HMAC key as hex bytes instead of UTF-8 text
tool.hash.options.keyHex.label: Key is hex
tool.hash.options.uppercase.label: Uppercase hex
